candidate_picture.profile_summary: Senior ML engineer with credible production, platform, RAG, streaming, monitoring, and leadership evidence; direct integrity and post-training depth is not yet demonstrated.

fit_assessment.label: LLM post-training depth
fit_assessment.boundary: The resume does not identify the method, dataset, evaluation, or individual ownership.

decision_state.reason: The candidate has strong adjacent production ML evidence, but the role-specific integrity and LLM post-training requirements are not yet supported by inspectable examples.

resume_guidance.why_it_matters: The target team protects the platform from content abuse and scaled attacks; general RAG and recommendation work does not prove that judgment.
resume_guidance.safe_direction: Add only candidate-confirmed integrity, trust-and-safety, fraud, anomaly, abuse, or adversarial evaluation work. If none exists, leave it as a preparation gap.
resume_guidance.truth_boundary: Do not relabel generic anomaly detection as abuse prevention without matching users, threats, labels, and decisions.
resume_guidance.completion_check: A reviewer can identify the threat model, data, model decision, failure cost, and measured result.

resume_guidance.why_it_matters: The posting names distillation, supervised fine-tuning, and policy optimization, while the resume says only 'fine-tuning techniques.'
resume_guidance.safe_direction: Replace the broad phrase with a candidate-confirmed method, dataset construction, objective, evaluation protocol, and trade-off, or remove the implication of depth.
resume_guidance.truth_boundary: Do not infer SFT, RLHF, DPO, distillation, or policy optimization from the generic fine-tuning phrase.
resume_guidance.completion_check: The candidate can defend the exact post-training method and explain why it was selected.

resume_guidance.why_it_matters: Senior interviewers will separate platform scope from the candidate's personal technical decisions.
resume_guidance.safe_direction: For SmartAssist, identify one architecture decision, one failed approach, one model-quality trade-off, and the candidate's direct ownership.
resume_guidance.truth_boundary: Keep team outcomes and individual contributions distinct.
resume_guidance.completion_check: The answer names the candidate's decision, alternatives, evidence, and consequence without expanding ownership.

strategy.positioning: Lead with production ML scale, model serving, evaluation, monitoring, and cross-functional ownership; treat integrity and post-training as explicit gaps rather than hiding them behind broad AI language.
strategy.application_posture: Apply as a credible adjacent candidate only after preparing a defensible integrity-system design and clarifying any real post-training work.
stop_rules: Do not claim integrity-domain experience without a candidate-owned threat or abuse example.
Do not convert fine-tuning into a named post-training method unless the candidate confirms it.
Do not use a numeric fit score or hiring probability for this case.

module_selection.label: ML integrity system design
module_selection.reason: The target owns platform-scale integrity systems, while the candidate has adjacent streaming, serving, and monitoring evidence but no direct abuse-system proof.

module_selection.label: Coding and algorithms
module_selection.reason: Reliable implementation is part of the engineering role; practice is narrowed to stream, graph, interval, heap, and window patterns that transfer to integrity workloads.

module_selection.label: Post-training and evaluation
module_selection.reason: The posting names post-training methods and the resume only claims unspecified fine-tuning, creating a direct proof gap.

module_selection.label: Applied AI implementation
module_selection.reason: The role combines models with production systems; an evaluation harness provides higher transfer value than a generic model demo.

module_selection.label: SQL and data reasoning
module_selection.reason: Data reasoning matters, but the current evidence gaps and likely ML depth have higher return within the 48-hour preparation limit.

module_selection.label: OOD / LLD
module_selection.reason: No supplied source makes object-oriented design a decisive screen for this target; system and implementation work already cover software judgment.

module_selection.label: Ownership and behavioral
module_selection.reason: The senior scope requires defensible personal decisions, failures, and cross-functional judgment, while current project ownership is underspecified.

question_factors.meaning: Does the question test an explicit requirement or likely round?
Could this gap materially block the candidate?
Will mastery help across adjacent AI and ML platform roles?
Can confirmed experience support a truthful answer or implementation?
Official format evidence outranks community reports; no leak frequency is claimed.

resource_factors.rule: Assign packaging, foundation, implementation, or production-depth material based on the diagnosed starting point.
Keep at most one framework, mechanism, production, and practice resource per path.
Specify exact scope, skip scope, time, and output; do not assign an entire site by default.
Primary sources establish mechanisms; the most learnable resource may establish the interview frame.

plan_factors.rule: High-risk gaps that recur across targets are scheduled first.
Mechanism learning precedes designs, implementations, and mocks that require it.
Every study block produces an artifact and later recall or mock.
The plan must fit 48 declared hours; SQL is deferred and OOD is suppressed in this case.

rounds.label: Recruiter screen
rounds.purpose: Clarify motivation, location, seniority, and whether the candidate's ML background maps to integrity work.

rounds.label: Coding and algorithms
rounds.purpose: Test data structures, implementation quality, complexity analysis, and reliable handling of edge cases.

rounds.label: ML and post-training depth
rounds.purpose: Test transformers, training objectives, dataset quality, fine-tuning, evaluation, and model failure analysis.

rounds.label: ML integrity system design
rounds.purpose: Design an abuse-detection system with data, modeling, serving, feedback, monitoring, and adversarial trade-offs.

rounds.label: Project and ownership deep dive
rounds.purpose: Separate personal decisions from project scope and probe failed approaches, measurement, and operations.

rounds.label: Behavioral and cross-functional ownership
rounds.purpose: Test judgment in ambiguity, competing priorities, disagreement, and end-to-end delivery.

interview_map.boundary: These are preparation-oriented round types inferred from the official requirements, not a confirmed OpenAI interview loop.

resources.title: OpenAI model optimization and fine-tuning guide
resources.why_it_fits: Provides an official workflow for dataset preparation, fine-tuning, and evaluation decisions.
resources.candidate_starting_state: Conceptually familiar but the exact SmartAssist method and evaluation are unconfirmed.
resources.reading_scope: Study when to fine-tune, data formatting, holdout evaluation, and iteration boundaries.
resources.skip_guidance: Skip provider-specific API syntax after you can explain the method-selection logic.
resources.assigned_output: One-page decision tree comparing prompting, RAG, and fine-tuning for the candidate's confirmed use case.
resources.completion_condition: Compare prompting, retrieval, SFT, and distillation for one integrity classifier scenario.

resources.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
resources.why_it_fits: Provides the primary technical basis for supervised fine-tuning, reward modeling, and policy optimization trade-offs.
resources.candidate_starting_state: The resume claims fine-tuning but does not prove post-training pipeline depth.
resources.reading_scope: Read the method, data-collection, reward-model, PPO, and evaluation sections; capture the pipeline and failure modes.
resources.skip_guidance: Skip exhaustive appendix tables on the first pass.
resources.assigned_output: A hand-drawn SFT → reward model → policy optimization flow with two failure modes and one integrity adaptation.
resources.completion_condition: Draw the SFT-to-reward-model-to-policy-optimization flow and name two sources of bias or reward misspecification.

resources.title: OpenAI safety evaluations hub
resources.why_it_fits: Shows how safety claims are paired with evaluation categories and explicit limitations.
resources.candidate_starting_state: Strong general evaluation experience but no confirmed adversarial misuse evaluation.
resources.reading_scope: Study evaluation categories, measurement boundaries, and how results are communicated.
resources.skip_guidance: Do not attempt to memorize every benchmark result.
resources.assigned_output: A three-layer offline, adversarial, and production evaluation scorecard for the integrity design.
resources.completion_condition: Define an abuse-evaluation suite with offline quality, adversarial coverage, and production monitoring layers.

resources.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
resources.why_it_fits: Provides a practical taxonomy for threats that an integrity system must detect or constrain.
resources.candidate_starting_state: Production ML background is adjacent, but an integrity threat model is missing.
resources.reading_scope: Focus on prompt injection, sensitive information disclosure, excessive agency, and unbounded consumption.
resources.skip_guidance: Skip implementation checklists unrelated to the chosen integrity-system design.
resources.assigned_output: A threat table mapping four abuse modes to signals, mitigations, residual risk, and alarms.
resources.completion_condition: Map four threats to signals, mitigations, residual risks, and measurable alarms.

resources.title: Google Rules of Machine Learning
resources.why_it_fits: Connects the candidate's proved production ML experience to data, serving, monitoring, and iteration decisions expected in the design round.
resources.candidate_starting_state: Production delivery is proved, but the interview story needs a clearer sequence of system and model decisions.
resources.reading_scope: Read rules 1–12, 21–28, and 32–39; focus on pipelines, first models, training-serving skew, feedback loops, and launch criteria.
resources.skip_guidance: Skip rules about organization-specific process that do not change the integrity-system design.
resources.assigned_output: Annotate the integrity architecture with five production ML risks and the stage where each is detected.
resources.completion_condition: Explain how data, training, serving, monitoring, and retraining fail independently and name one guardrail for each.

resources.title: AWS Builders' Library: Using load shedding to avoid overload
resources.why_it_fits: Adds a concrete production deep dive for overload, fairness, and graceful degradation in a real-time classifier path.
resources.candidate_starting_state: The candidate has scalable pipelines but the runbook lacks evidence of overload policy and degradation judgment.
resources.reading_scope: Read the sections on overload detection, request prioritization, load shedding, retry amplification, and testing.
resources.skip_guidance: Skip service-specific implementation details after the policy and failure interactions are clear.
resources.assigned_output: Add overload signals, tenant priorities, retry budgets, and fail-open/fail-closed decisions to the integrity design.
resources.completion_condition: Defend when the classifier path sheds, queues, degrades, or fails closed under three overload scenarios.

resources.title: OpenAI evaluation best practices
resources.why_it_fits: Turns the candidate's general LLM evaluation claim into a concrete dataset, grader, regression, and failure-analysis workflow.
resources.candidate_starting_state: Evaluation experience is claimed and partially proved, but the implementation and release-gate details are not visible.
resources.reading_scope: Read eval design, dataset construction, grader choice, continuous evaluation, and failure analysis examples.
resources.skip_guidance: Skip SDK syntax until the evaluation contract and test cases are written with a fake model client.
resources.assigned_output: A typed evaluation contract, ten-case golden set, two graders, and a release-gate rule.
resources.completion_condition: Implement the harness with deterministic tests and explain grader disagreement, leakage, and regression thresholds.

resources.title: LeetCode Top Interview 150
resources.why_it_fits: Provides implementation practice, but the assignment is narrowed to the patterns used by the selected integrity-flavored questions.
resources.candidate_starting_state: The candidate has strong systems experience but no supplied evidence of recent timed algorithm practice.
resources.reading_scope: Use only hash map, sliding window, heap, intervals, graph traversal, and design-a-data-structure sections; complete one new and one spaced-repeat problem per session.
resources.skip_guidance: Skip dynamic programming, advanced math, and unrelated hard problems during this six-week plan.
resources.assigned_output: Eight tested solutions, a pattern map, and an error log with 48-hour and seven-day retries.
resources.completion_condition: Solve two unseen medium variants in 35 minutes each with clarification, tests, and complexity analysis.

question_bank.prompt: Your background is strongest in production ML and RAG. Why move into platform integrity now?
question_bank.why_asked: Tests motivation without assuming direct integrity experience.
question_bank.selection_reason: Priority A because the transition is visible from the resume and will determine whether adjacent experience sounds intentional or opportunistic.
question_bank.candidate_relevance: Production ML and evaluation are proved; integrity motivation is a missing candidate fact.
question_bank.completion_standard: Deliver a 90-second answer that names verified strengths, the honest gap, and one concrete preparation artifact.

question_bank.prompt: Implement a bounded event counter that detects abusive burst patterns while handling late events.
question_bank.why_asked: Connects algorithms and reliable implementation to the target domain.
question_bank.selection_reason: Selected over generic array drills because it covers sliding windows, ordered state, eviction, late data, and testability in one integrity-adjacent problem.
question_bank.candidate_relevance: Streaming systems are proved, so the candidate can connect implementation choices to known event-processing constraints.
question_bank.completion_standard: Implement in 35 minutes with API clarification, late-event policy, bounds, tests, and complexity analysis.

question_bank.prompt: Walk through the exact fine-tuning method used in SmartAssist, including data, objective, evaluation, and failure cases.
question_bank.why_asked: The resume uses a broad phrase that may not prove post-training depth.
question_bank.selection_reason: Priority A because it directly tests the largest claimed-versus-proved discrepancy in the resume.
question_bank.candidate_relevance: SmartAssist is the strongest adjacent project, but its method, data, evaluation, and ownership are unconfirmed.
question_bank.completion_standard: Either produce a fact-checked five-minute method narrative or remove the unsupported implication from the resume.

question_bank.prompt: Design a real-time system that detects coordinated content abuse at platform scale.
question_bank.why_asked: Tests the most important role-specific gap.
question_bank.selection_reason: Priority A because one design covers the target's integrity domain while reusing the candidate's proved streaming, serving, and monitoring strengths.
question_bank.candidate_relevance: The architecture primitives are adjacent and proved; threat modeling, labels, human review, and attacker adaptation remain gaps.
question_bank.completion_standard: Deliver a 35-minute design plus 15 minutes of follow-ups on coordination signals, class imbalance, privacy, drift, and rollback.

question_bank.prompt: How would you evaluate a classifier when attackers adapt and the positive class is rare?
question_bank.why_asked: Tests adversarial evaluation, calibration, cost trade-offs, and monitoring.
question_bank.selection_reason: Selected because it converts the unknown adversarial-evaluation gap into a transferable evaluation problem rather than asking for nonexistent experience.
question_bank.candidate_relevance: General monitoring is proved, creating a truthful bridge to rare-class and adaptive-adversary trade-offs.
question_bank.completion_standard: Define offline slices, precision-recall costs, adversarial holdouts, delayed labels, online guardrails, and retraining triggers without notes.

question_bank.prompt: Tell me about an ambiguous ML problem where you changed direction after production evidence contradicted the original plan.
question_bank.why_asked: Tests end-to-end ownership and learning under uncertainty.
question_bank.selection_reason: Priority B because the resume proves team outcomes but needs one candidate-owned decision that survives senior-level follow-ups.
question_bank.candidate_relevance: The candidate has monitoring and leadership evidence, but the specific decision, failed hypothesis, and consequence are not documented.
question_bank.completion_standard: Give a six-minute STAR-L answer with personal decision, contrary evidence, alternative, measured consequence, and three follow-up answers.

question_bank.prompt: Maintain the top K abusive actors over a sliding time window with bounded memory.
question_bank.why_asked: Tests hash maps, heaps, window eviction, and correctness under updates.
question_bank.selection_reason: Adds a second implementation pattern without duplicating the late-event counter: ranking and stale heap entries are the new mechanisms.
question_bank.candidate_relevance: Streaming experience provides a truthful bridge to window and state trade-offs.
question_bank.completion_standard: Implement in 35 minutes, explain exact versus approximate alternatives, and test ties, eviction, and repeated updates.

question_bank.prompt: Given account-event links, identify suspicious coordinated components above a configurable threshold.
question_bank.why_asked: Tests graph construction, traversal, component statistics, and scale-aware reasoning.
question_bank.selection_reason: Introduces the graph pattern that the first two stream questions do not cover and maps directly to coordinated-abuse language.
question_bank.candidate_relevance: The domain is a preparation gap, so the answer must stay at design and implementation level rather than imply experience.
question_bank.completion_standard: Build and traverse the graph correctly, state complexity, test isolated and duplicate edges, and discuss streaming approximation.

question_bank.prompt: Build a testable evaluation harness for an integrity classifier using a fake model client and configurable graders.
question_bank.why_asked: Tests production-quality AI implementation rather than notebook-only model knowledge.
question_bank.selection_reason: Selected because it turns the candidate's evaluation claim into code with interfaces, deterministic tests, failure paths, and release criteria.
question_bank.candidate_relevance: The resume names an LLM evaluation framework but does not expose its contract, graders, or regression behavior.
question_bank.completion_standard: Implement typed inputs, fake client injection, two graders, timeout handling, aggregate metrics, and deterministic tests in 90 minutes.

question_bank.prompt: Design the human-review and feedback loop for uncertain integrity decisions without creating label leakage or reviewer overload.
question_bank.why_asked: Tests the operational system around the model, not only classifier architecture.
question_bank.selection_reason: Adds human operations, active sampling, reviewer quality, and feedback-loop risk that the main architecture question may otherwise underdevelop.
question_bank.candidate_relevance: Cross-functional delivery is proved, but human-review system design is not.
question_bank.completion_standard: Define queues, prioritization, reviewer calibration, disagreement, privacy, appeals, label delay, and learning-loop safeguards.

question_bank.prompt: How would you choose and change an enforcement threshold when false positives harm legitimate users?
question_bank.why_asked: Tests calibration, cost-sensitive evaluation, staged rollout, and policy judgment.
question_bank.selection_reason: Selected as the decision-focused complement to the broader adaptive-attacker evaluation question.
question_bank.candidate_relevance: Monitoring experience supports metrics reasoning; integrity-specific failure costs remain a preparation gap.
question_bank.completion_standard: Explain cost matrix, calibration, slice analysis, shadow launch, guardrails, appeals, and rollback with one numerical example.

question_bank.prompt: Tell me about a technical disagreement where you changed the decision process rather than merely winning the argument.
question_bank.why_asked: Tests senior cross-functional influence and decision quality.
question_bank.selection_reason: Adds an influence story distinct from the production-learning story and targets the proved leadership evidence that still lacks a specific mechanism.
question_bank.candidate_relevance: Mentoring and KPI collaboration are proved, but conflict, alternatives, and decision mechanisms are not documented.
question_bank.completion_standard: Give a six-minute story covering positions, shared criteria, evidence, decision mechanism, result, and what changed afterward.

outline: start from verified production ML and model-quality work
explain the specific integrity problem that motivates the transition
show the preparation artifact and learning plan
state only the method actually used
name one failed approach and trade-off
define abuse actors, protected users, decisions, and latency
design event ingestion, labels, features, model, rules, and human review
cover class imbalance, coordinated attacks, feedback loops, and privacy
define offline metrics, online guardrails, drift detection, and rollback

phases.label: Evidence repair
phases.rationale: Resolve the two claims most likely to undermine credibility before adding broad interview coverage.
phases.exit_gate: SmartAssist wording is fact-checked and the candidate can deliver the integrity design without implying production abuse ownership.

actions.title: Audit the SmartAssist fine-tuning claim
actions.artifact: One-page SmartAssist method and evidence audit
actions.exit_gate: Every method, dataset, metric, and ownership statement is either confirmed or explicitly removed.
actions.completion_condition: Produce a one-page method, data, objective, evaluation, ownership, and limitation brief using only confirmed facts.

actions.title: Design a coordinated content-abuse detection system
actions.artifact: Architecture diagram, threat model, evaluation scorecard, and 35-minute talk track
actions.exit_gate: Complete two timed runs and answer five adversarial follow-ups without claiming prior integrity ownership.
actions.completion_condition: Deliver a 35-minute design covering threats, data, labels, model/rules, serving, review, evaluation, monitoring, privacy, and rollback.

phases.label: Interview depth
phases.rationale: Expand only after the credibility blockers are repaired; mix mechanism study, implementation, and retrieval practice.
phases.exit_gate: Three consecutive mocks meet the completion standards for coding, ML depth, design, and ownership.

actions.title: Build a post-training comparison map
actions.artifact: Post-training comparison map and five-minute verbal explanation
actions.exit_gate: Choose between prompting, RAG, SFT, distillation, and policy optimization for two scenarios and defend the trade-offs.
actions.completion_condition: Compare prompting, RAG, SFT, distillation, and policy optimization across data, cost, evaluation, and failure modes.

actions.title: Practice integrity-flavored coding problems
actions.artifact: Eight tested solutions plus an error and retry log
actions.exit_gate: Two unseen medium variants are completed in 35 minutes with tests and correct complexity analysis.
actions.completion_condition: Solve and explain eight medium problems spanning hash maps, heaps, intervals, graphs, streams, and sliding windows with tests and complexity analysis.

actions.title: Prepare the SmartAssist ownership deep dive
actions.artifact: Twelve-minute project deep dive with architecture and follow-up bank
actions.exit_gate: The story separates personal and team work and survives three ownership and failure follow-ups.
actions.completion_condition: Give a 12-minute narrative with architecture, personal decisions, failed approach, metrics, incident/rollback, and two trade-offs.

application_experiment.hypothesis: Explicitly positioning verified production ML strengths while disclosing integrity and post-training gaps produces more useful recruiter feedback than generic AI keyword matching.

cohorts.name: adjacent-integrity-roles
cohorts.purpose: Test whether the evidence-bounded positioning is credible for roles where production ML is core and integrity is learnable.

application_experiment.success_signal: Qualified human feedback that identifies the same strengths and gaps, not application volume or a promised response rate.
